text: So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Then Solomon brought in the gifts his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and all the vessels—and placed them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, that is, Zion.
All the men of Israel gathered to the king at the festival in the seventh month.
When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark.
They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites carried them up.
King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered with him before the ark sacrificed sheep and cattle too many to be counted or numbered.

versions.text: King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered with him before the ark sacrificed sheep and cattle beyond counting or numbering, so many were they.
versions.explanation: The trailing clause "so many were they" is a somewhat clumsy addition after "beyond counting or numbering"; a single clause renders מֵרֹב more smoothly for oral reading.

text: The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, so that they overshadowed the ark and its carrying poles from above.
The poles were so long that their ends could be seen extending from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, though they were not visible from outside. And there they remain to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.

versions.text: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בְּצֵאתָם is temporal ("when they came out"), not sequential ("after"); and the relative clause attaches most naturally to Horeb as the place of the covenant.

text: Then the priests came out of the Holy Place. All the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions,

and all the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and kinsmen—stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, and with them a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets.

The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making a single sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. As they lifted up their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and instruments of music, they praised the LORD: "He is good; his mercy endures forever." Then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,

versions.text: The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making a single sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. As the trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments rose in song, they praised the LORD: "He is good; his mercy endures forever." Then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says they "lifted up the voice" with the trumpets, cymbals, and instruments; the current wording makes the instruments themselves the subject that "rose in song," which is both imprecise and slightly awkward for reading aloud.

text: and the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
